1. Framework: All data loading, preprocessing, model training, and evaluation MUST use the LensKit library directly (not OmniRec, RecBole, or other frameworks).

2. Datasets: Load exactly three datasets: MovieLens 100K (via lenskit.data.load_movielens), Amazon Video Games (via lenskit.data.load_amazon_ratings or from_interactions_df with appropriate data), and Last.FM (via from_interactions_df with appropriate data).

3. Preprocessing - Implicit binarization: For MovieLens100K and Amazon Video Games, convert ratings > 3 to implicit interactions (ratings > 3 become 1, others removed) using DatasetBuilder.binarize_ratings() with min_pos_rating=3 and method='remove', or equivalent logic.
4. Preprocessing - 5-core filtering: All three datasets MUST undergo 5-core filtering (remove users and items with fewer than 5 interactions) after any binarization.

5. Data splitting: Use sample_users() from lenskit.splitting with SampleFrac(0.2) for a user-based 80/20 holdout split. No validation set is required. Generate exactly 5 different splits by passing different random seeds (e.g., seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4) via the rng parameter.

6. Algorithms: Test exactly three algorithms from LensKit: ImplicitMFScorer (from lenskit.als), ItemKNNScorer (from lenskit.knn), and PopScorer (from lenskit.basic). All algorithms MUST use default/standard hyperparameters.

7. Training & Recommendation: For each algorithm, build a top-N recommendation pipeline via topn_pipeline(), train on the train split, and generate recommendations for the test users using BatchPipelineRunner.
8. Evaluation metrics: Compute NDCG and Precision at k=1, 5, 10 using lenskit.metrics.ranking.NDCG(n=k) and lenskit.metrics.ranking.Precision(n=k) via RunAnalysis.add_metric().
9. Experimental design: For each combination of dataset (3) × algorithm (3) × seed (5), train on the training split and evaluate on the test split, yielding 45 total experiment runs.

10. Statistical analysis: After collecting results, compute mean and standard deviation of each metric across the 5 seeds for each (dataset, algorithm, k) combination to quantify the impact of random seed variation on accuracy.
